newsitem.title: UK: IRA could still be brought to peace talks - Major.
newsitem.headline: IRA could still be brought to peace talks - Major.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday that the IRA was more isolated than ever but could still be brought to Northern Ireland's negotiating table.

Speaking to pupils during an election campaign stop at Pangbourne, west of London, Major said he believed peace was achievable in the troubled British province despite the Irish Republican Army's resumption of violence in February 1996.
The renewed attacks, which followed a 17-month ceasefire, dashed hopes for any quick settlement in the province.
But Major said Anglo-Irish efforts to secure peace had helped to isolate "the violent men of the IRA and cost them much of the support they had around the world".

"They are much more isolated today in their belief that violence can succeed than they have probably ever been in their history. And for that reason, I think we will be able to draw them into talks on terms satisfactory to the other political parties and then proceeed toward a settlement," he said.

Multi-party talks in Northern Ireland have been suspended pending Britain's general election on May 1. Major is considered a rank outsider to win re-election but the talks are due to resume anyway on June 3.

The Conservative leader said the talks had made little progress to date, partly because of the "wickedness" of the IRA in resuming violence and partly because some parties -- he did not say which -- had been reluctant to take risks for fear of alienating their supporters in the run-up to an election.
Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA, could only take up a seat at the negotiating table if the IRA laid down its arms once and for all, Major said.
"I believe there is a way through to get all the parties to sit down together and talk provided there is a clear-cut and verifiable ceasefire by Sinn Fein and the IRA ," Major said.
The U.S. administration, which has played a leading role in efforts to bring a lasting peace to Northern Ireland, has also been increasing the pressure on the IRA to resume talks and abandon warfare.
Bringing peace to Northern Ireland has long been one of Major's personal goals, an ambition he reiterated on Wednesday as the campaign -- possibly his last -- got under way.
"There is nothing in politics I would like to achieve more than a conclusive settlement in Northern Ireland," he said.
